title: Manager shadow slate rubric and boarding template
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working template used by People Ops + Hiring Managers to: (1) run a manager shadow slate for cross-functional candidates, (2) capture structured interview scoring for paired interviews, and (3) surface a 30/60/90 onboarding template tailored for managers that will own IC teams. Aim is to reduce variability between hiring panels and speed up onboarding once offer is accepted.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for non-executive manager roles (IC+1 to mid-level managers) where cross-functional collaboration and operational delivery matter.
- Best paired with a calibrated hiring slate (3–5 candidates) where candidates are given a short shadow window with 2 teams.
- Not intended for director+ or deep individual contributor roles.

High-level flow (one-pager):
1) Prep (People Ops + Hiring Manager) — 3 days before slate: confirm rubric, shadow hosts, interviewers, and candidate brief.
2) Shadow session — 1/2 day per candidate: 60–90m observed time split across 2 teams + 30m debrief with HM.
3) Interview panels — same day or next: paired technical/business/people interviews using standardized scorecard.
4) Calibration sync — hiring manager + interview leads: same day. Decision window: 48 hours.

Shadow session structure (suggested):
- 10m candidate intro + expectations (People Ops host)
- 25–30m observational block with Team A: candidate observes team standup/code review/product planning; small task or critique prompt optional.
- 25–30m observational block with Team B: different lens (eng ops, product, or support).
- 15–20m private conversation with hiring manager focused on role-specific situational discussion.
- 20–30m panel debrief (interviewers only) — collect initial notes and scores.

Interview rubric (calibration primers):
Scoring scale: 1–5 (1 = no evidence, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = exceptional)
Core dimensions (each dimension should have 1–2 example evidence prompts):
- Team leadership & coaching (prompt: describe a time you developed a lower-level engineer)
- Execution & prioritization (prompt: how do you settle tradeoffs when roadmap slips)
- Technical judgment (prompt: system design for X, read code and suggest improvement)
- Cross-functional influence (prompt: give example of aligning product + infra)
- People ops partnership & bar-raising (prompt: hiring decisions, performance conversations)
- Role fit & mission alignment (prompt: why Redwood and what would you change in week 1)

Rubric guidance notes:
- Interviewers should capture 1–2 behavioral anchors for each score (e.g., "3 = ran consistent 1:1s with documented development plan; 4 = measurable promotion outcomes").
- Avoid grading on technical trivia; focus on pattern recognition and outcomes.
- For internal candidates, add a field for "context of previous team" to avoid bias.

Scorecard template (one-line per field to paste into interview form):
- Candidate name:
- Role:
- Interview date:
- Interviewer:
- Scores: leadership (1–5), execution (1–5), technical (1–5), cross-functional (1–5), ppl-ops-partner (1–5), fit (1–5)
- Written evidence: 6 short bullets capturing specific examples
- Red flags (Y/N + notes)
- Recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / Consider / No hire

Calibration checklist (for HM + interview lead):
- Are scores correlated across interviewers? If variance >2 points on core dims, convene quick follow-up interview or assign a tie-breaker reviewer.
- Confirm role must-haves vs. nice-to-haves before final decision.
- Document any compensation exceptions or relocation needs.

30/60/90 onboarding template (manager-tailored)
Notes: this is intentionally outcome-driven and oriented to first 90 days after offer accept. Share with candidate at offer stage to set expectations.
- Week 0 (pre-start): hardware, access, org chart, 1:1 schedule for first 30 days, intro emails drafted, stakeholder list, first-week reading list.
- Days 1–30 (Discover): attend core team rituals, 1:1s with direct reports (initial listening plan), meet cross-functional partners, review existing roadmaps/KPIs, quick wins (deliverable: run first project post-mortem).
- Days 31–60 (Align & Act): set team goals and ownership mapped to company objectives, establish 30–60 day success metrics for direct reports, begin active hiring or role reshapes if needed, lead first planning cycle end-to-end.
- Days 61–90 (Scale & Improve): start performance calibration, implement at least one process improvement (e.g., release cadence, onboarding checklist for new ICs), present working plan to VP.

Manager onboarding checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Offer letter signed and counter-signed
- [ ] Manager kickoff packet sent (org chart + 1:1 templates)
- [ ] Hardware provisioned and VPN/KMS access requested
- [ ] First 8 1:1s scheduled with direct reports
- [ ] People Ops scheduled 30/60/90 checkpoints on calendar
- [ ] Hiring queue and scorecard templates shared
- [ ] Access to Redis/Observability dashboards + billing view if applicable

Communication templates (short):
- Pre-start intro email to team: short script included in appendix
- 1:1 cadence template: 30m weekly for first 30 days, agenda items prioritized as: 1) concerns, 2) goals, 3) career development.

Common FAQ / edge cases:
- If a candidate misses a scheduled shadow day, allow one reschedule within 7 days; beyond that, withdraw from slate.
- For internal transfers, accelerate decision timeline to 72 hours, ensure skip-level manager signs off.
- If calibration shows strong disagreement, bring in a neutral senior interviewer (not previously involved) for tie-break.

Appendix: sample behavioral anchor table (copy-paste friendly)
- Leadership 5: repeatedly promoted direct reports; has documented mentoring curriculum and measurable team growth
- Leadership 3: runs regular 1:1s and has provided development plans; inconsistent promotion outcomes
- Execution 5: drove multi-quarter projects with clear impact metrics across org boundaries
- Execution 3: delivered projects on time most of the time; relied on direction for scoping

Next steps (People Ops owners):
- Run a 1-hour calibration workshop with all hiring leads to adopt this rubric (target: within 2 weeks).
- Pilot this template with the next manager hire in Q4 and gather interviewer feedback via a short survey.
- Iterate templates and push final copy to Confluence after 2 pilot hires.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and written for quick copying into Drive interview forms. Open to suggestions on extra dimensions we should capture (e.g., DEI adjustments, remote-first signals).
